sonnet.problem: The right answer, 'The deceitful tongue', was already shown as part of the right answer on card 4 ('Lying lips and a deceitful tongue'). The question also adds that the psalmist 'stops praying to the LORD', which the text does not say.
sonnet.rule: An answer shown on one card, right or wrong, isn't used again on a later card.

sonnet.problem: The question asks what the arrows and burning coals 'are about' and treats them as what is coming to the deceitful tongue. Verse 4 never says what the picture stands for or how it connects to verse 3. The question also already says the tongue is asked what will be done to it, so the right answer is nearly given away.
sonnet.rule: This includes what a picture means. He retells the picture as the text gives it and says what it stands for only when the passage says so.

sonnet.problem: The wrong answer 'gold' is not believable for what people 'want' in this verse. It is out of place beside 'war' and 'quiet', so it reads as silly and is easy to rule out.
sonnet.rule: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.
